points.body: At that time, Kálii Bhat́cáj was in Kashii. A grandfather also has a grandfather. So there was also someone who could overrule Kálii Bhat́cáj. For so long, Kálii Bhatcáj had been spending his days quite happily and peacefully. Whenever necessary, he would be absent for eight to ten days from the office without obtaining any leave. Sometimes, he would simply hang his coat on the chair and go home. He instructed the attendant, “If the boss comes, just tell him that I have gone to the bathroom. And in the meantime, you call me at my home.” Kálii Bhat́cájʼs senior officials who came to visit him were all red-faced Englishmen. So he had no difficulty going on leave because those Englishmen were not familiar with the customs and conventions of this country. Whatever Kálii Bhat́cáj told them, they took it as gospel truth. But life does not always flow smoothly. Finally, an Indian became Kálii Bhat́cájʼs boss. He knew all the local customs. Once, on coming to enquire about Kálii Bhat́cáj, he found him absent from the office. On asking the Establishment Clerk, he came to know that there was no application for leave from Kálii Bhat́cáj. He then issued a ‘show cause chargesheet’ against Kálii Bhat́cáj.

points.body: In the following three days, nothing happened. During those three days, Kálii Bhat́cájʼs beard had grown a little. Kálii Bhat́cáj came to the office barefoot. Needless to say, he had heard the rumour about the chargesheet but did not know the details. As soon as he reached the office, the Establishment Clerk narrated everything to him. When everyone saw Kálii Bhat́cájʼs mahágurunipátdashá ( 2 ) [formal mourning signs with unshaven beard and bare feet] on the death of his parent, they understood why Kálii Bhat́cáj had been absent from the office. After hearing what the Establishment Clerk had to say, Kálii Bhat́cáj gave a wry smile on his emaciated face and remarked, “How can I blame my boss? He does not know about my misfortune.”

points.body: With due respect, I, your humble servant, would like to state that I belong to a family of high caste (kuliin) Brahman of Shantipur. My grandfather, the late Shataratha Bhattacarya, had one hundred wives. ( 3 ) Every third day, my grandfather would go to one of his wives to collect obeisance money. Thus he spent three hundred days. For the remaining sixty-five days, he stayed at home and examined the account of the proceeds from the obeisances and looked after the farm. My grandfather died long ago. My grandmothers are also following suit singly or in twos. Three died last year and this year, five have already passed away. Possibly because it is colder this year, they are dying in greater numbers. However, sir, I have stated the truth. Up till now, twenty-two grandmothers have gone to heaven (with a remaining seventy-eight grandmothers yet to die).”

points.body: In Sanskrit, the verbal root ras means to call by creating a special type of sound; second, to flow; and third, to be sticky. Suppose you are here and on the other side of the vast field stands Khudua Mahato. How would you call him? You will shout, “Oh, Khudua Mahato … ohhhhhhhhh....” To be carried means to flow, to move slightly like a drop of water on a lotus leaf. The third meaning is to feel sticky. For example, glue or mango gum. In all three cases we obtain the word rasa from the verbal root ras. Because of the presence of this juice or rasa, a particular kind of sweet is called rasagollá [round-shaped juicy sweet made of fresh cheese]. There are other such sweets – rasamálái and rasabaŕá.

points.body: One day, Kyáblákánta thought of keeping all his money intact by taking up the “style of a python”. Perhaps you know what is the “pythonʼs style”. Keeping its mouth wide open, it moves very fast so that all kinds of animals and insects enter straight into its stomach. When its stomach is fully gorged, it shuts its mouth and then hibernates for one week, sometimes for a fortnight if necessary. After the food is digested, it starts to move again. Humans are said to adopt the python style when they move about with the intention to take whatever comes their way.

He passed one field after another; nothing else came within his sight. Kyáblákánta with the heavy bag of wealth on his shoulders tottered onwards. The goat was bleating in his stomach, creating a serious problem. He must reach some shelter before dark. By and by, a town appeared. After going some distance, he saw a huge house with a flower garden in front and a fruit garden at the back. But how could it be? Such a big house and not a single light was on! points.body: The government servant said, “Look, I am the caretaker of the house. You can stay here with my permission. But the particularity of this house is that during the day, there is no problem staying in it; once night falls, there is danger. As soon as the sun goes down, ghosts appear and they make life hell for the guest with their various dances and songs. Occasionally, in the past some high-ranking government officers and ministers sought permission to stay here in order to enjoy film songs and cabaret dances. I granted them permission. But at the last moment, they cancelled their stay out of fear that female spirits would break their necks. Since then, the king has made a rule that if anybody wants to spend a night in this house, he must sign a risk bond – that in the event of his death he himself will be responsible but if by good luck he survives – then the king will not only give him half the kingdom but also his daughter in marriage if the horoscopes and other conditions are found suitable.”

Then he went to the king and demanded half the kingdom. It is a road on which if you walk fast for a few days, you will quickly reach the huge gate of hell. The male and female ghosts that you meet on the way will only encourage you to move along.”

Not only the ghosts on either side of the road, but also his forgotten friends and relatives were telling him, “You have done the best thing, the right thing. Walk faster. This road to hell is the road of the intelligent and the intellectuals. Eat whatever you like; donʼt be choosy. We also ate according to our inclinations. As a result, some of us died of cholera and some of diabetes. Even after coming here, we have been eating whatever we feel like. We have indulged unrestrainedly in intoxicants and we have died of liver cirrhosis. After arriving here, we are continuing the same practice. This is known as the path of pleasure. Here, the custom is: eat, drink and be merry, for life is short. We are happy to see you. As soon as you reach hell, we shall make you a member of our infernal club.”

When he saw Kyáblá, he motioned his assistants to go forward to welcome him with a garland of cowdung cakes. The ghost told Kyáblákánta, “In the smithy, you gave me a beating with the hammer. Come, come inside, then you will see how I shall bring you to book.”

In the sentence, “Rama, what are you saying?” the word “Rama” is used in the vocative case. Again, if I say, “What is Rama saying?”, with a pause between “What is” and “Rama”, then “Rama” is used in the nominative case. In this connection, you must have heard of this well-known story.

Since he was going to inherit the huge property of his aunt after her death, he anxiously looked forward to the day when she would die. But his aunt was not dying at all. Harekrśńa became impatient. Some wicked people said that one night, he murdered his aunt. There was a police enquiry and lawsuits. Many villagers said that they had heard the old lady shouting at the top of her lungs, “I am being murdered! Oh, I am being murdered by Hare!”

points.body: In the normal course of events, the case would have been filed against Harekrśńa. Harekrśńa sought the help of a famous lawyer. The lawyer told the court, “Yes, of course, it is certainly true that at the time of her death, the old lady shouted, ‘Iʼm being murdered by Hare!ʼ Harekrśńa was the only relative of the old lady. Harekrśńa was her only hope and support. Those wicked villagers who had possibly heard the old lady shouting at the time of her death, ‘Iʼm being murdered by Hare!ʼ actually killed the old lady. In that situation, whom could the old lady call for help? She naturally called her nephew, her only support, and shouted, 'Hare ámáy márle!ʼ [Hare, Iʼm being murdered!] In other words, she wanted to say, 'Hare! Please come and see me, people are killing meʼ. She called ‘Hare’ only with the hope that Hare would come to her rescue. In this case, the old lady used the word ‘Hare’ not in the nominative case but in the vocative case.”

Since there was a little pause between the two words Hare and ámáy [me], people mistakenly thought that the old lady was saying that it was Hare who was trying to murder her. However, the lawyer, by distancing the word ámáy from Hare in articulation, convinced the judge of Hareʼs innocence.

points.body: We use the Sanskrit verbal root lup to mean breaking up. When we prepare a programme for a certain event, we divide the time into certain parts or periods. This kind of programme or breaking up of time is also called la. Intelligent human beings apply la to all their work. A good housewife, after lighting the stove, completes the tasks of cleaning the utensils, washing the rooms and other similar work. When the stove is ready, she will first boil the food that takes a long time to cook, then in the meantime she will complete other tasks such as cutting the vegetables, grinding the spices, taking her bath and worshipping. When there is a proper sense of la or organization, human life is fully enriched. Then the work done within oneʼs short, limited life assumes a rich significance, and the drama of life becomes a grand success. Otherwise, even a long life gets lost in darkness from sheer futility. Do you know the story of the weaving couple?

points.body: Once, there was a weaver and his wife. The wife never felt pressed for time in her housework. After firing the stove, she would do some weaving. After putting the rice pot on the stove, she would do some dyeing. After she had finished cooking and feeding her husband, she would go to the marketplace to sell some clothes, and on her way back she would buy groceries from the market. Not only did she do all the household chores, she wove and sold clothes as well. All the villagers were full of praise for her. And that was not all. Whenever anyone was in trouble, she would help them to the best of her ability. She could not afford to help financially but would give her own food instead. The villagers respected and loved her. They called her Vidyádharii.

This process of wearing down would have ultimately affected the entire body. That means there would have remained nothing like a body.”

He only knew that a song originates in a particular collocation of sound. So, while walking. he kept his ears alert. Suddenly, he heard the very sweet, gentle sound of something falling quietly. For so long, he had been under the impression that he was the richest man in the village and Bokendranáth was the poorest. But, today, what strange sights he had seen with his own eyes! Bokendranáth was carelessly throwing money away in the streets. He must have a huge amount of money at home stored in big, earthen containers.
